Hub C out-connects its neighbors and tops the table at 0.19, while A and the pendant G have better-connected neighbors and score negative, -0.27 and -0.33." width="100%"} Leverage centrality measures the degree connectivity of a node relative to its neighbors: `leverage(v) = (1/k_v) · Σ[(k_v - k_n) / (k_v + k_n)]` where `k_v` is the degree of node `v`, and `k_n` is the degree of each neighbor `n`. Interpretation: - positive values: node has more connections than its neighbors (influential) - negative values: node has fewer connections than its neighbors (peripheral) - zero: node has similar connectivity to its neighbors ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name for the node attribute to store results. If not provided, auto-generates name from method name (`leverage_centrality`). [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary of results. If `False`, stores results as node attributes and returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to leverage centrality scores. If `return_dict=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The hub has positive leverage, since its degree far exceeds that of its low-degree neighbors, while each leaf has negative leverage for the opposite reason: ::: {#c2db4273 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["hub", "A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("hub", "A"), ("hub", "B"), ("hub", "C")]) ) graph.leverage_centrality(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {3: -0.5, 1: 0.5, 4: -0.5, 2: -0.5} ``` ::: ::: Storing the result as a node attribute lets it chain directly into visualization methods like `colorize_node_attrs()`: ::: {#0c3f62cf .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["hub", "A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("hub", "A"), ("hub", "B"), ("hub", "C")]) ) ( graph .leverage_centrality(attr_name="leverage") .colorize_node_attrs( node_attr_from="leverage", node_attr_to="fillcolor", palette="RdBu" ) .describe() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Number of nodes : 4 Number of edges : 3 Directed : False Density : 0.50 Average degree (min, max) : 1.50 (1, 3) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : True Bipartite : True Computations: - leverage_centrality() -> attr: 'leverage' (4 of 4 nodes) Node aesthetics: - fillcolor <- leverage via colorize (palette: "RdBu") (values: #b2182b, #d6604d, 4 of 4 nodes) ``` ::: :::
